title: Consistency models: retrieval check
markdown:
## Recall before you check

This retrieval pass revisits consistency models without re-teaching them. Before opening the check, say in your own words what linearizability promises about a single object across all clients, how sequential consistency weakens that, what causal consistency preserves and what it lets differ, what read-your-writes and monotonic reads guarantee for one session, and why eventual consistency is a liveness statement rather than a safety one.

## What to bring back

- Linearizable: every operation appears to take effect atomically at some instant between its start and finish, in one real-time order for all clients.
- Sequential: one total order that respects each client's program order, without the real-time requirement.
- Causal: operations that are causally related are seen in the same order everywhere; concurrent operations may be seen in different orders.
- Session guarantees: read-your-writes (a session sees its own writes), monotonic reads (a session never sees older state after newer state).
- Eventual: if writes stop, replicas converge; it says nothing about what a read returns meanwhile.
- Stronger models cost coordination and availability under partition; weaker models shift the reasoning to the application.

Answer from memory first, then read the feedback.

key_takeaways: Linearizability adds a real-time order that sequential consistency does not require.
Causal consistency orders related operations everywhere and lets concurrent ones differ.
Session guarantees are per client; eventual consistency only promises convergence.

questions.prompt: A write completes at 10:00:00; a read starting at 10:00:01 on another client returns the old value. Which model does this violate?
questions.explanation: Linearizability requires the read, which started after the write finished, to observe it.

questions.prompt: Which guarantee ensures a user sees their own just-submitted comment on the next page load?
questions.explanation: It is a session guarantee about a client observing its own writes.

questions.prompt: Two unrelated writes on different keys are seen in different orders by two replicas. Which model still holds?
questions.explanation: Concurrent, causally unrelated operations may be ordered differently under causal consistency.

choices: Every read returns the latest write
Reads are monotonic within a session
questions.explanation: It is a convergence promise, not a statement about individual reads.

questions.prompt: A session reads version 5, then version 3 of the same object. Which guarantee is broken?
questions.explanation: A session must not observe older state after newer state.
